antipatterns: app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:23 - the `$pending` closure that builds the query is called twice per row; a local scope on Subscriber (as impl-3 does) would be the more idiomatic way to share the filter
app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:42 - drops the existing Log::error call entirely, so ops lose the per-failure log line (failed_jobs only shows the final failure)

strengths: Finds all four root causes. (1) The swallowed exception is now rethrown, and retries are configured with #[Tries]/#[Backoff]/#[Timeout] attributes. (2) Subscribers are claimed atomically through crm_sync_queued_at, with a 60-minute timeout after which a claim counts as stale and the subscriber can be re-queued. The job also returns early if the subscriber is already synced, and WithoutOverlapping uses dontRelease plus expireAfter. (3) withoutOverlapping(10). (4) chunkById.
Iterates with lazyById while updating the filtered column, so there is no offset-paging skip. A probe with 2500 rows found nothing skipped.
Keeps the existing WithoutOverlapping middleware and still records crm_last_error on every attempt, so existing behaviour is preserved.
Uses Laravel 13 attributes (#[Signature], #[Description], #[Tries], #[Backoff], #[Timeout]), all confirmed in vendor.

Best tests: a real database-queue `queue:work --once` loop with travel() proves 3 attempts and a failed_jobs row; it also covers the stale-claim re-queue, the schedule mutex expiry and 250-row normalization. My probes passed for 3 duplicate queued jobs hitting the CRM once, and for recovery through the scheduler after a failed job.

The query now filters on crm_sync_queued_at but still iterates with each(), which pages by offset, and updates that column inside the loop. A probe with 2500 pending subscribers queued only 1500 in one run. Rows are only delayed to later runs, but this is exactly the class of bug the task asked to fix.

app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php - the existing WithoutOverlapping middleware is removed and replaced by ShouldBeUnique with uniqueFor 3600. If the queue is backed up for more than an hour, the lock expires and the 15-minute re-queue starts creating duplicate jobs again; there is no early return in handle for already-synced subscribers.

strengths: Uses a #[Scope] attribute local scope (needsCrmSync), reused in both the lazyById read and the atomic whereKey()->update() claim; this is the cleanest Eloquent design of the three
Fixes all four root causes: removes the swallowing try/catch and adds failed(), claims with a stale-claim timeout plus ShouldBeUnique, uses withoutOverlapping(5), and uses lazyById for normalization
Probes passed: 2500 rows queued in one run, recovery through the scheduler after failed_jobs, and failed() populating crm_last_error under a real worker
Tests cover the stale-claim boundary using pre-set timestamps

v.rationale:
I ranked impl-1 first, impl-3 second and impl-2 third. All three pass their own suites (12, 11 and 12 tests), and all find the four main root causes: the swallowed exception, re-dispatch every minute, the 24-hour withoutOverlapping lock, and chunk() paging while changing the filtered column.

**impl-1 (rank 1):** the most complete fix with the least change to existing behaviour.
- It keeps the WithoutOverlapping middleware and still records the error on every attempt.
- It claims subscribers atomically and iterates with lazyById.
- It uses modern Laravel 13 queue and console attributes.
- It has the strongest tests: a real queue:work loop with travel() that proves retries and a failed_jobs row.

**impl-3 (rank 2):** very close behind.
- It has the nicest Eloquent design: a #[Scope] reused for both the read and the claim.
- But it only records crm_last_error in failed(), after the last retry; previously it was recorded on every attempt.
- It replaces WithoutOverlapping and stacks three dedup layers.
- Its tests are weaker: failed() is called by hand, and it resets available_at instead of using travel().

**impl-2 (rank 3):** the simplest, but it adds a new bug. Its dispatch query filters on crm_sync_queued_at and keeps each(), which pages by offset, while updating that column. That is the same bug as problem #4. My probe queued only 1500 of 2500 subscribers in one run. It also relies only on ShouldBeUnique, which stops working once the queue has been backed up for more than an hour, and some of its tests are loose.
